headline: Computational annotation of mass spectrometry data across peptides and metabolites
label: Untargeted Metabolomics Annotation Tools
summary: Enhanced spectral library search and isotope-based identification tools address annotation accuracy in high-resolution mass spectrometry datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational identification of analytes from high-resolution mass spectrometry data, with the strongest methodological overlap between the two tool papers. The enhanced ANN-SoLo engine unifies spectral library search with Prosit-predicted libraries, spectrum-level and peptide-level decoys, and complementary ion vectors to support open modification searching. MIMI instead identifies metabolites in UHR-FT-ICR data by matching peaks to theoretical isotopic variants of stable isotope-labeled compounds, operating as a command-line tool. The TMT-based SureQuant study addresses a parallel problem of sensitivity and multiplexing, using super heavy TMT triggers to quantify histone H3 PTMs in single cells. What is new across these items is the coupling of predicted reference spectra and decoy-based control to search strategies, and the use of isotopic pattern matching for ultra-high-resolution metabolite annotation.
